question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 12 hours, pipe B can fill the same tank in 25 hours and pipe C can fill the same tank in 10 hours. The time taken by them to fill the same tank if they operate together is::
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work (LCM of 12, 25, 10) = 300 units.

Efficiencies: A = 25, B = 12, C = 30.

Combined Efficiency = 25 + 12 + 30 = 67.

Time Taken = 300 ÷ 67 = 4(32/67) hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 4(32/67) hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Pipe A fills in **12 hours**, Pipe B in **25 hours**, and Pipe C in **10 hours**.

**Formula Used:** Total Work = Time × Efficiency

 
 **Person** **Days** **Total Work** **Efficiency** 
 Pipe A 12 300 25 
 Pipe B 25 12 
 Pipe C 10 30 

⇒ Sum of efficiencies of (A + B + C) = 25 + 12 + 30 = **67 units/hr**

⇒ Total Time Taken = Total Work ÷ Total Efficiency

⇒ Time = 300 ÷ 67

⇒ Time = 4(32/67) hr

**∴ The correct answer is 4(32/67) hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Logic

Filling pipes have **positive efficiency**, while outlet/leakage pipes have **negative efficiency**.

Time and Work Relation

Time is inversely proportional to efficiency: **Time = 1 / Efficiency** when work is constant.</p
